label: copy-phase input i, early in the copy of short sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the token fed back in is the letter i (99.9% of activation mass is on input i). It never fires during the original phase or on the delimiter. Within copy-phase i inputs it fires sparsely (about 10% of them). It favours early recall positions (recall_idx 1-3, peaking at 2, i.e. the i was original token 0-2 and was just echoed back) in short sequences (L 3-5) where only 1-2 outputs remain. The strongest activations are on i echoed right after <DEL> or one step after it, in L=3-4 sequences, often followed by o or 0. Magnitude drops as L grows; the feature is near-silent for L>=7. It does not respond to any other input token. Precision is limited because many early i inputs in L=5-6 sequences stay inactive.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: i, o, 0, -, g, c; least: y, 1, n, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: 0, o, i, g, a, f; least: k, v, s, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=2, L=3 & t=4, L=3.
